title: Plastics - 123 school
heading: Plastics
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: Name two types of polymerisation reaction
questions.a: Condensation polymerisation and addition polymerisation

questions.q: What is the polymerisation reaction that involves double bonds called?
questions.a: Addition polymerisation

questions.q: What is the polymerisation reaction in which H<sub>2</sub>O is released called?
questions.a: Condensation polymerisation

questions.q: Name the three steps of an addition reaction in which a polymer is formed
questions.a: Initiation, propagation, termination

questions.q: Which molecule is needed in a hydrolysis reaction?
questions.a: Water (H<sub>2</sub>O)

questions.q: In which reaction do radicals play the main role?
questions.a: Addition reaction/addition polymerisation

questions.q: Name two bonds that are typical of condensation polymerisation
questions.a: Ester bond, amide bond

questions.q: Does the reaction of ethanoic acid and ethanol in the presence of sulfuric acid produce a polymer?
questions.a: No, because ethanoic acid has only 1 carboxyl group and ethanol only 1 hydroxyl group, so as soon as they form an ester bond with each other the reaction stops.

questions.q: Does the reaction of benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid (A) and ethane-1,2-diol (B) in the presence of sulfuric acid produce a polymer?
questions.a: Yes, because after the reaction of 1 of the 2 carboxyl groups of A with 1 of the 2 hydroxyl groups of B, the ester compound formed still has 1 carboxyl group and 1 hydroxyl group left to react further

questions.q: Why is sulfuric acid added to a condensation reaction?
questions.a: Protons are needed to form H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>, which is needed to react with the double-bonded O and start the reaction.

questions.q: Is sulfuric acid consumed overall during the condensation reaction?
questions.a: No, the proton that binds first is given up again in the last step of the formation of the ester bond

questions.q: What is a copolymer?
questions.a: A polymer that has been formed from different monomers

questions.q: From which monomers can you form polyesters?
questions.a: A dicarboxylic acid and a diol, or from hydroxy acids

questions.q: From which monomers can you form polyamide?
questions.a: A dicarboxylic acid and a diamine, or from amino acids

questions.q: Which typical groups does an amino acid have?
questions.a: –NH<sub>2</sub> and –COOH

questions.q: Which typical groups does a hydroxy acid have?
questions.a: –OH and –COOH

questions.q: What is benzoyl peroxide used for in an addition polymerisation?
questions.a: As an initiator. When the peroxide (–O–O–) bond is split (e.g. by heating), radicals form that start the polymerisation reaction

questions.q: Polymerisation reactions of benzoyl peroxide and ethene form a poly....
questions.a: Polyethene

questions.q: Which bond is important in the polymerisation of ethene?
questions.a: The double bond

questions.q: Which repeating unit forms in the polymerisation of ethene?
questions.a: -CH<sub>2</sub>-CH<sub>2</sub>-

questions.q: In the production of polyethene, benzoyl peroxide is built in. Do you find this back in the abbreviation of the polymer, and why?
questions.a: No, because it is at the ends of the polymer and has no influence on the properties of the polymer

questions.q: What are thermosetting plastics (thermosets)?
questions.a: Polymers that stay hard when heated

questions.q: What are thermoplastics?
questions.a: Polymers that become soft when heated

questions.q: Name the typical differences between thermosets and thermoplastics
questions.a: Thermoplastics are chains that lie next to each other and do not form a network. In thermosets the chains are connected to each other: they are cross-linked

questions.q: What does the flexibility of a thermoplastic depend on?
questions.a: Possibly side chains and their size; the degree of polymerisation; the presence of plasticisers
